correctness.rationale: The Alexander-dual cover consists of simplices indexed by forbidden full stars; all nonempty intersections are simplices, and its equivariant nerve is the codimension-two simplex skeleton. The full-simplex boundary sequence computes the integral top nerve lattice as sign times permutation/diagonal; integral UCT identifies its dual with the augmentation kernel. The signed equivariant Alexander duality calculation contributes the edge permutation sign, which equals sign^(n-2); the final tensor is sign^(n-1) times the augmentation lattice. All degrees, n=3, orientation actions, and torsion-free assertions are controlled. An independent exact finite signed trace and mod-two rank verifier passed.

originality.rationale: Anurag Singh (arXiv:2006.13632, v1 2020-06-24), particularly Theorem 1.1 and section 3, determines wedge dimensions but not S_n lattice actions. Wachs (2003) pp.24–29 reproduces Reiner–Roberts rational module decompositions for bounded-degree graph complexes that explicitly allow loops, not the loopless edge universe of this result, and does not identify the integral S_n lattice here. Targeted web and published mathematical-results searches for the complex, sign/augmentation duality, equivalences and broader representation coverage found no statement implying this precise integral identification. The absence of hits is not a uniqueness proof; a differently formulated loopless antecedent remains possible.
residual_risks: Older bounded-degree graph-complex work may admit a special loopless reduction not explicitly stated in the inspected general loop-allowing formulations.
An unindexed exact integral S_n-lattice identification or later equivariant specialization to M_{n-2}(K_n) may exist.
Finite verification cases check traces and mod-two homology, not the universal integral group-lattice isomorphism.

value.rationale: The subject is the natural action of all vertex relabelings on the precise family of higher-matching complexes whose n−1 sphere homotopy type was established by Singh. The integral lattice distinguishes augmentation from its non-isomorphic integral dual, tracks the parity-dependent sign, and yields subgroup-fixed dimensions for all H≤S_n. Neither an abstract wedge count nor a rational character alone supplies the integral representation. The Alexander-dual nerve supplies structural rather than census-only information.
